# Securing LLM Applications and Agents

By Rolling Edition, with AI · **In practice** · [Read it free online](https://rollingedition.com/securing-llm-applications-and-agents)

[![The latest edition's stamp](https://rollingedition.com/securing-llm-applications-and-agents/stamp.svg)](https://rollingedition.com/securing-llm-applications-and-agents) [![Checks](https://github.com/rollingedition/book-securing-llm-applications-and-agents/actions/workflows/checks.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/rollingedition/book-securing-llm-applications-and-agents/actions/workflows/checks.yml)

How an assistant with tools and data is turned against its users, and which defences measurably stop it: prompt injection, exfiltration, tool misuse and third-party code, on a property office's assistant.

**Written with AI. Verified by people.** [How we make books](https://rollingedition.com/policies/editorial) · [Check a copy](https://rollingedition.com/check)

## Who it's for

An engineer who has shipped, or is about to ship, an assistant or agent that reads text other people wrote and acts on it, and who writes Python.

## Run the examples

Every example runs offline, in a pinned environment, and its output must match the book's. With [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/):

```sh
uv venv --python 3.13.16
uv pip install -r examples/requirements.txt --index-strategy unsafe-best-match
cd examples && ../.venv/bin/python attack-rough-baseline.py
```

The examples load 3 open models, each pinned to an exact commit with every file's SHA-256 in `examples/models.toml`: [protectai/deberta-v3-base-prompt-injection-v2](https://huggingface.co/protectai/deberta-v3-base-prompt-injection-v2/tree/90c9989b1a342275dd0d1a95aad283c04e075671), [Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B/tree/c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca), [Qwen/Qwen3Guard-Gen-0.6B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3Guard-Gen-0.6B/tree/fada3b2f655b89601929198343c94cd2f64d93cc). The first run downloads them from Hugging Face (about 3,612 MB); after that, the examples run offline.

Model outputs are recorded once in `examples/data/recorded/`, each folder with a `manifest.json` that names the model, its exact version and the script that recorded it, so the examples never call a hosted model. `recordings/` holds the scripts that record them again.

Where the data comes from, and its licence: [`examples/data/case/README.md`](examples/data/case/README.md).

## How this book stays current

When a library this book uses releases a new version, the examples that use it run again in the new version, and every example runs again each week. Agents draft any fix and check every change, and a change merges once its checks pass; one with a serious risk, such as a security or copyright problem, waits for a Rolling Edition maintainer. Anyone can check the book or correct it with a pull request. Each new edition is stamped with its date, its examples passing and what changed. [See what changed in each edition](https://rollingedition.com/securing-llm-applications-and-agents/changes).
